newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Pasminco eyes lower break-even costs.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Pasminco eyes lower break-even costs.

text.p: Mining and smelting group Pasminco Ltd said it on Friday its acquisition of Australia's giant Century zinc mine would aid in lowering the company's overall break-even zinc price.
Trevor Shard, company secretary for Pasminco, told the Macquarie Bank Ltd zinc symposium that studies were underway to reduce the development cost of the Century.
Pasminco has said it would look to trim development costs by about 10 percent.
Shard did not disclose what the studies had revealed to date.
Excluding the Century mine, Pasminco, which has been targeting a break-even price of US$850 a tonne and so far has whittled costs to US$895 a tonne, Shard said.
"We've been working toward that for about two years," Shard said.
Development of Century, one of the world's largest untapped zinc mines, would take the break-even price even lower, Shard added.
The roughly A$1 billion figure was based on an assessment by the current owner, RTZ Corp Plc-CRA Ltd.
RTZ-CRA has agreed to sell the mine to Pasminco pending the finalisation of native title land claims hanging over the project.
Pasminco earlier this year paid a A$10 million deposit on the mine and has agreed to pay a balance of A$335 million if the deal proceeds.
Shard said Pasmico held undrawn credit lines adequate for the acquisition and that the total project would be funded by a mix of debt and equity.

Shard also said development of Century, which would supply about half its annual output to Pasminco's wholly-owned Budel smelter in the Netherlands, could be used as a supply source to expand its Risdon zinc smelter in Hobart, Tasmania.
"We are looking at what we can do, particularly at Pasminco's Hobart smelter," Shard said.
